title: The Legacy of the Observer
next_chapter_hook: The remnant soul of the First Observer whispered, in a voice only Chen Ji could hear, before dissipating: "Beyond the Tianji Record, there exists a fourth possibility... that is the choice erased by the Heavenly Dao itself."

text.content: Chen Ling's terrifyingly calm voice still echoed in his ears—"In these three years, who do you think has been bearing the Heavenly Dao's gaze for you?" These words were like a blunt blade, slowly dissecting all his自以为是的 calculations. Three years. He thought he had been advancing steadily under Tianji Record's protection, never knowing that the one truly shielding him from wind and rain was his sister Chen Nian, whom he had regarded as a chess piece. At this moment, Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill—not from external threat, but from his deep disgust at his own foolishness.

dialogue.content: The guardian of the remnant soul's voice drifted from the depths of the Tianji Record, carrying an unprecedented weight: "What she said is true. What the little girl has endured all these years is not merely the Heavenly Dao's gaze... That is karmic backlash, the price of every glimpse into the future through the Tianji Record, which should have been borne by the user."

text.content: Chen Ji raised his head sharply, a flash of astonishment in his eyes, immediately replaced by an even deeper coldness. He should have realized—every consumption of Heavenly Fate Value was accompanied by some formless transfer of karma. He had always believed the Tianji Record was bearing the burden for him, but now it seemed the one truly承接那些因果 was his sister, whom he had left in Chen Family Village, thinking she was safe. At this moment, emotions like anger, self-blame, and guilt surged like a tide, but Chen Ji suppressed them, turning them into a barely perceptible fierce gleam at the bottom of his eyes.

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, as if deliberating how to speak, before finally continuing: "Some things shouldn't be told to you now. But since the little girl has already revealed them... Chen Ji, do you know who the original master of the Tianji Record was? Why was it created?" The remnant soul's voice became ethereal, as if recalling some distant past, "The Tianji Record is not some ancient secret treasure, but rather—"

text.content: Before the words finished, the first page of the Tianji Record suddenly glowed with a ghostly blue light—a color Chen Ji had never seen. Within the light, a blurry figure slowly coalesced. The figure was incomplete, like ink wetted by water, its edges constantly blurring and reforming, yet emanating a heart-stopping威压. Chen Ji's pupils contracted—this aura, he had sensed it in Mo Xiansheng's occasionally泄露 emotions, but never so strong, so... heroic.

dialogue.content: "The First Observer..." Mo Xiansheng's voice was rare带上了 trembling, "Why do you manifest at this moment?" The blurry figure seemed to hear his words and slowly turned its head. Though the face was invisible, Chen Ji clearly感知到一道目光落在自己身上—that gaze held no blame, only a近乎温柔的审视, as if looking at a junior who had finally grown up.

The figure spoke, its voice aged yet gentle, like the last warmth of winter sunlight: "Junior, no need to自责. Every Observer is a survivor who crawled out of the Heavenly Dao's chess pieces. You think you have calculated every possibility, but you were already in the game the moment the Tianji Record chose you." The figure paused, its tone gaining more释然, "But the game is not a死局. The true purpose of the Tianji Record was never to let you peek into the future... but to give you the possibility to change."

text.content: Chen Ji listened quietly, his expression unchanged, but his heart was掀起惊涛骇浪. For three years, he had regarded the Tianji Record as a tool to peek into the future, each foresight accompanied by the consumption of Heavenly Fate Value, each consumption making him more dependent on this ability. He never thought the original purpose of creating the Tianji Record was not to窥命, but to—change. These two words were like thunder, splitting open a thick fog in his mind.

dialogue.content: Just then, Su Qingyao's voice came from outside the door, carrying压抑的 anxiousness: "Chen Ji, are you in there? Just now during my cultivation, I suddenly had a感应... as if something was calling to me, that feeling was just like..." She didn't finish, but Chen Ji noticed that the First Observer's figure trembled slightly upon hearing her voice.

text.content: The First Observer's figure slowly turned toward the door, and an expression of complex emotion seemed to appear on that blurry face: "The bloodline of the Fate Chronicler... has not been severed after all." His voice held more sentiment, "When I entrusted the Tianji Record to the Observer lineage, I left a暗线—if ever a Daughter of Fate appeared beside an Observer, it would be the day our fire of传承 was passed. Boy, she is your fortune, and also your calamity."

choice.prompt: The remnant soul of the First Observer was dissipating, his words carrying profound meaning. At this moment, Chen Ji needed to make a choice—

choices.description: Choose to proactively bear the mission and karma left by the First Observer, no longer letting Chen Nian alone承受 the Heavenly Dao's gaze. This is a path of sacrifice, but also the only way to save his sister.
choices.visible_cost: Consume a large amount of Heavenly Fate Value, proactively ignite karmic backlash
choices.visible_reward: Obtain all memory fragments of the First Observer, unlock the "Observer's Eye" skill

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and walked slowly toward the dissipating figure. He didn't hesitate, didn't speak unnecessary words, only reached out his hand to touch that bundle of fading light. The moment of contact, a burning current rushed through his entire body from his fingertips, countless images flickering past like a carousel—the life of the First Observer, the struggles and falls of countless Observers, the true secrets of the Tianji Record. Pain rushed in like a tide, Chen Ji groaned, blood flowing from the corner of his mouth, but his eyes were clearer than ever.

dialogue.content: "Good... good a后生!" The First Observer's figure trembled violently, yet emitted a relieved laugh, "You didn't ask me why I wanted this, didn't ask if it was worth it... you simply chose to bear. This determination alone surpasses many of the past Observers!"

choices.description: Not rush to bear karma, but first extract more key intelligence from the First Observer. A user of the Tianji Record never fights unprepared battles—what he needs is information, not sentiment.
choices.visible_cost: Miss the best inheritance timing, the First Observer's remnant soul accelerates dissipation
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key clues about the "Fourth Possibility"
choices.risk_hint: May lose the complete Observer inheritance

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his outstretched hand, stepping back half a pace, his face wearing its usual composed expression: "What the senior has said, the junior will keep in mind. But before inheriting this legacy, I dare to ask—if the true purpose of the Tianji Record is to change, then what exactly does this change point toward? And what is this fourth possibility?" His tone was calm, yet his gaze was as sharp as a blade, directly targeting the heart of the matter.

dialogue.content: The figure of the First Observer paused slightly, then let out a low laugh, carrying both commendation and bitterness: "A fine young one who won't strike until seeing the rabbit... very well, since you've asked, the old man will speak a bit more." His voice suddenly dropped, becoming ethereal and dangerous, "The Tianji Record documents three fates—heaven's way, altering fate, and defying heaven. But there's a possibility never recorded in its pages. It's the fourth choice obliterated by the heavens themselves, a forbidden path the old man pursued his entire life yet never truly reached."

choices.text: Enduring in silence, gathering strength, biding the time
choices.description: The First Observer's words made Chen Ji realize the situation was far more intricate than he had anticipated. He opted for temporary restraint, refusing to hastily accept this karmic burden, and decided to wait until he fully comprehended its advantages and disadvantages before making any choice.
choices.visible_cost: The First Observer's remnant soul dissipated due to waiting, missing the complete transmission
choices.visible_reward: Preserving the complete Heavenly Fate, retaining room for future choices
choices.risk_hint: Potentially losing the opportunity to obtain the complete transmission forever

text.content: Chen Ji did not speak, merely watching that gradually vanishing figure in silence. He neither reached out nor pressed further questions, instead carving every word and expression of the First Observer into the deepest recesses of his mind. Sometimes, not making a choice is the best choice. He, Chen Ji, had never lacked patience. Three years ago, he could endure in silence as worthless trash; in the future, he could wait with even deeper scheming for that optimal moment.

dialogue.content: The First Observer's figure seemed to see through his thoughts, showing no disappointment but instead a meaningful smile: "Enduring, gathering strength, borrowing power, plotting schemes... You're more like a true Observer than I was in my youth. But remember, lad—the Tianji Record chose you not because of your calculations, but because of your..." Before the words finished, the figure scattered like dust, leaving only the final word echoing in the air, "Heart."

text.content: As that figure vanished completely, the Tianji Record returned to silence. But Chen Ji could clearly perceive that this ancient,残破 tome seemed to have undergone some subtle change—it had become more weighty, as if bearing more memories and destiny. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out once more, this time carrying unprecedented solemnity: "The First Observer chose you. This is the first time in the Tianji Record's recorded history that it has manifested proactively in a remnant soul state. What he left you is not merely a transmission, but a... trust."

dialogue.content: Outside the door, Su Qingyao's voice sounded again, this time with more unease: "Chen Ji, my premonition is growing stronger... as if something is calling me to a certain place. It said..." She paused, hesitating whether to speak, "It said the descendant of the Fate Scribe has finally arrived."

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze flickered sharply. The Fate Scribe—the bloodline inheritance mentioned just now by the First Observer—had actually sought out Su Qingyao. This was no coincidence. He rapidly organized the information in his mind: Su Qingyao had always harbored suspicions about him, approaching the truth three times only to be deflected three times. Now that the Fate Scribe's power was awakening within her, what did this mean? Opportunity, or crisis? Chen Ji would not forget what the First Observer had said—Su Qingyao was both his opportunity and his catastrophe.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao sensed destiny's call, and Chen Ji had just acquired partial transmission from the First Observer. At this moment, he must make a decision—

choices.description: Chen Ji decided to appear before Su Qingyao as a worthless junior brother, to probe the extent of her awakening. This could both soothe her unease and allow him to secretly observe the developments.
choices.visible_cost: Revealing his absence from the room might trigger a new wave of suspicion from Su Qingyao
choices.visible_reward: Close-range observation of Su Qingyao's awakening state to obtain first-hand intelligence
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao was already astute; at this moment, her sensory abilities might be even sharper

text.content: Chen Ji straightened his robes and pushed open the door. Su Qingyao stood at the corridor's end, her complexion pale under the moonlight, with faint flowing light flickering between her brows—that was a sign of the Fate Scribe's bloodline awakening. He strode forward quickly, donning his usual honest smile: "Senior Sister Su, visiting so late at night—is something wrong?" His tone was solicitous, but his eyes swept across her brow in the first instant, recording every detail of that flowing light.

dialogue.content: When Su Qingyao saw him, her expression eased slightly, yet puzzlement remained: "During my cultivation just now, I sensed a voice... it said I am a descendant of the Fate Scribe, and that it had finally waited for me." She stared directly into Chen Ji's eyes, her gaze lacking its usual scrutiny, instead carrying a trace of dependence she herself had not noticed, "Chen Ji, can you tell me what's going on?"

choices.description: Chen Ji chose to remain hidden, observing Su Qingyao's reactions. He needed to confirm whether this was a genuine bloodline awakening or some kind of trap directed at him. After all, in this turbulent world, any sudden stroke of fortune could be fatal.
choices.visible_cost: Missing an excellent opportunity to build trust with Su Qingyao
choices.visible_reward: Avoiding stepping into a possible trap, gaining a more objective observational perspective
choices.risk_hint: If Su Qingyao encounters danger, the optimal rescue timing will be lost

text.content: Chen Ji didn't push open the door. Instead, he concealed his presence and observed silently through the window crack. Su Qingyao stood under the moonlight, the stream of light gradually stabilizing. Her expression shifted from initial panic to contemplative thought. He noticed that whenever the stream of light flickered, she would unconsciously look toward where he was hiding—as if something was guiding her closer. A chill ran through Chen Ji's heart as the first observer's words surfaced in his mind again: She is your fortune, and also your doom.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji, I know you're in there." Su Qingyao's voice suddenly rang out, calm and certain. "Every time you hide from me, your breathing becomes much quieter. Did you think I couldn't tell?" She let out a soft sigh, her tone carrying an unexpected hint of resignation. "Come out. I won't interrogate you about anything. It's just... I need someone to help me figure this out."

text.content: In the end, Chen Ji pushed open the door. Not because Su Qingyao's words had moved him, but because he clearly understood—at this critical moment, any deliberate distance would only make an already suspicious person even more vigilant. Besides, the first observer had personally said that Su Qingyao's bloodline had some destined connection to his own. Since this connection was unavoidable, he might as well proactively incorporate it into his own chess game. Chen Ji walked slowly toward Su Qingyao, the moonlight stretching their shadows long across the ground, intertwining them like some silent omen.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao gazed at the approaching Chen Ji, her eyes complex with mixed emotions. Three years ago, when she first noticed this servant disciple, she had thought he was no different from the usual waste. But at some point she couldn't pinpoint, she had begun to sense an inexplicable dissonance in this person—his gaze was too calm, his reactions too composed, his deference before the strong too perfect. Perfect to the point of... resembling a meticulously crafted performance. "Chen Ji," she spoke softly, her voice carrying a tenderness she herself hadn't realized, "thank you for coming out."

text.content: Chen Ji paused slightly. Su Qingyao's attitude toward him seemed to have undergone some subtle change without his noticing. From initial scrutiny and suspicion, to later vigilance and probing, and now this... indefinable gentleness. This wasn't a good sign. Trust too easily gained often conceals the deepest traps. He lowered his eyes, hiding the flash of alertness without a trace, and replaced it with a simple, honest smile: "Sister Su, you're too kind. It's this junior's honor to be of help."

choice.prompt: Facing Su Qingyao's rare softness, Chen Ji needed to make a choice between sincerity and pretense—

choices.text: Partial sincerity, leaving room to maneuver
choices.description: Chen Ji decided to add some genuine elements to this performance. He told Su Qingyao partial truths—about the Tianji Record, the observers, and the possible connection between their bloodlines. Not everything, but enough to let her feel his sincerity.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing part of his trump cards would put Chen Ji at a disadvantage if Su Qingyao had ulterior motives
choices.visible_reward: Greatly increase Su Qingyao's trust and favor, paving the way for future 'shared destiny' buffs
choices.risk_hint: Trust is a double-edged sword—used well, it's a boost; used poorly, it's a disaster

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, as if making some difficult decision. Finally, he raised his head, his gaze losing some of its usual timidity and gaining a rare seriousness: "Sister Su, there are things I shouldn't tell you, but since we've both been drawn into this whirlpool... perhaps honest communication gives us better odds than mutual suspicion." He paused, lowering his voice. "Do you know that the Tianji Record is no ordinary cultivation technique?"

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's pupils contracted slightly. She stared intently at Chen Ji's eyes, as if trying to read every truth from those deep pools. After a moment, she nodded lightly: "Continue." Her tone was calm, yet a tremor in her voice was unmistakable—that was anticipation, and also fear. Three years of investigation, countless probes—finally, the moment for answers had arrived.

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyes, wearing an expression of bewilderment: "The Fate Writer? Sister, I'm not very clear about this either... I've only heard that the Tianji Record seems to be an ancient secret treasure, something about divining the future. But how would a servant disciple like me understand such things?" His tone carried just the right amount of fear, while his eyes inadvertently swept across the light between Su Qingyao's brows, recording every detail in his mind.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao watched him silently, her gaze as if trying to see through his entire being. After a long moment, she sighed softly: "Chen Ji, you know what? What I hate most is this way of yours—always keeping yourself watertight." Her voice was soft, yet carried a strange weariness. "Fine, if you won't say, I won't force you. It's just..." She paused, raising her hand to touch her brow center. "This thing probably won't disappear just because I don't want to know about it."

text.content: Just as the atmosphere fell into a subtle stalemate, the Tianji Record suddenly grew warm. Chen Ji's heart stirred as a thought transmitted from the ancient, damaged book—it was Mo Xiansheng's voice, carrying a hint of urgency: "The transmission from the first observer is complete, but his final words, I didn't have time to relay just now." Chen Ji dealt with Su Qingyao with an unchanged expression, while asking in his heart: "What words?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent for an instant, as if weighing his words: "He said—the Fate Writer bloodline within Su Qingyao is the only key by which you might escape the fate bound to the Tianji Record. But whether to use this key or not must be your own choice."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. Escaping the fate of the Tianji Record—this was a possibility he had never imagined. Every use of the Tianji Record consumed Heavenly Fate Value, and the moment Heavenly Fate Value was exhausted was the moment the user was completely devoured by the Heavenly Dao. He had always believed this was a path of certain death, that all he could do was delay the arrival of death, and before death descended, lay out as many schemes as possible and plan as deeply as he could. But the first observer had actually told him there was another path? A path to completely escape fate? Chen Ji's heartbeat couldn't help but quicken, but his face remained utterly calm.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji?" Su Qingyao's voice pulled him back from contemplation. She noticed his momentary absentmindedness just now, and a flash of understanding crossed her eyes: "What are you thinking? Are you considering whether to tell me the truth?" She smiled lightly, the smile carrying a hint of self-mockery. "Rest assured, I won't force you. Three years, I've chased you for three years. Every time I thought I was about to catch your tail, you would skillfully slip away. I'm tired..." Her voice gradually dropped. "Perhaps there are some things it's better not to know. That itself is a kind of happiness."

text.content: Night wind brushed past the corridor, lifting a few strands of blue-black hair by Su Qingyao's temples. Under the moonlight, her face shed its usual cold hardness, revealing a startling fragility. Chen Ji watched her silently, and somewhere in his heart, something seemed to be gently touched. For three years, he had always regarded Su Qingyao as one of the greatest threats, using every means to defuse her every probe. But at this moment, looking at this woman's exhausted expression, he suddenly realized—she too was just an ordinary person caught up in fate's current, just like him. The first observer had been right—Su Qingyao was both his fortune and his doom. But perhaps... fortune and doom are merely the two sides of the same coin.
